Lehre Forschung Organisation

186.814 Algorithmics
This course is in all assigned curricula part of the STEOP.
This course is in at least 1 assigned curriculum part of the STEOP.

2026W, VU, 4.0h, 6.0EC
  • TUWEL course

Properties

  • Semester hours: 4.0
  • Credits: 6.0
  • Type: VU Lecture and Exercise
  • LectureTube course
  • Format: Hybrid

Learning outcomes

After successful completion of the course, students are able to...

This module deals with advanced algorithmic methods and their theoretical analysis for solving complex computational problems.

Students gain comprehensive knowledge of algorithm design principles and analysis techniques. They learn to develop theoretical solutions for computational problems and prove their correctness using mathematical methods.

Students acquire the ability to abstract problems into formal models and develop and analyze algorithmic solutions through mathematical reasoning. Furthermore, students will be able to identify, articulate, and discuss issues concerning ethics, gender and diversity in the context of the module’s content.

Subject of course

This module covers advanced algorithms and data structures and algorithm analysis. It has an emphasis on (but is not limited to) algorithms on graphs and methods for problem solving and optimization. The module consists of a lecture together with exercises.

Topics covered

  • Computational complexity
  • Planarity of graphs
  • A* algorithm
  • Randomized algorithms
  • Linear and (mixed) integer linear programming
  • Parameterized algorithms and kernelization
  • Graph decompositions and treewidth
  • Geometric Algorithms

Teaching methods

Introduction and explanation of general methods, discussion of examples, justification by giving formal arguments and proofs, independent problem solving, presentation and discussion of solutions.

Mode of examination

Immanent

Additional information

Organization

The course is divided by topics into six blocks, each consisting of three lectures and one exercise.
The final grade will be based on the exercises and on two written exams. There are six mandatory units of exercises.
All lectures, exercises, and exams are held in person, but lectures and exercises are also recorded and provided online as far as possible.

The first lecture takes place on Monday, October 5, 10:15-11:45 in EI5. It includes a presentation of the course organization.

Exercises

For each of the six lecture blocks, a corresponding exercise sheet will be provided in TUWEL. You are expected to solve the stated tasks and to submit your solutions in PDF via TUWEL by certain deadlines within about one to two weeks after each lecture block. We will check a selected portion of all submissions. Joint exercise classes will take place on Thursday 29.10., 5.11., 19.11., 3.12., 10.12. and 14.1. at 15:15-16:45 in different rooms. In these classes, the lecturers will show selected solutions to each exercise task and discuss them with you. While it is not mandatory to participate in these exercise classes, we strongly encourage you to use this opportunity to learn and ask questions.

Exams

There will be two written exams (~90 min each) that take place on November 27, 14:00-16:00 and January 21, 10:00-12:00. The first exam will cover the content of lecture blocks 1–3, the second that of lecture blocks 4–6. Additionally, there will be the possibility to do or repeat one of the two exams or both on March 18, 16:00-20:00. If you take one of the exams twice, the later result counts. You must take exams on both lecture parts for a positive grade.

Grading

The mark you receive depends on the two exams (each 35%) and your performance in the exercises (30%).
Exercises will influence your grade via the total number of tasks you indicate to have accomplished and submitted before the deadlines and which we found in our checks to be acceptable.

The minimal requirements for a positive grade are:

  • Each of the 6 exercise sheets consists of 8 tasks. For at least 5 out of 6 exercise sheets, you must solve at least 3 out of 8 tasks. These have to be marked and successfully submitted in TUWEL (both) by the specified deadlines as well as accepted by our checks.
  • ≥50% are required on each written exam.
  • ≥50% overall.

To obtain full points for the exercise portion of the grade, it is sufficient to (correctly) solve ≥75% (i.e., 36 out of 48) of the exercise tasks.

Overall grade distribution:
S1: [88%,100%]
U2: [75%,88%)
B3: [63%,75%)
G4: [50%,63%)
N5: [0%,50%)

Note: Once you have submitted solutions for at least one exercise you will in any case receive a grade at the end of the term.

Course material

Lecture slides will be available in TUWEL.
